scheme_name: PRISM (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs): Category-1: Proof of Concept/ Prototypes/ Models
description:
The PRISM scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2020. 

It is specifically aimed at promoting innovations in individuals, start-ups, and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). 

The scheme is designed to support the development of proof of concept, prototypes, and models. 

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is the implementing authority for this scheme. 

The primary objective of PRISM is to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the MSME sector. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to innovators and entrepreneurs to develop their ideas into viable products. 

Under this scheme, the government aims to support at least 1,000 innovative projects annually. 

The financial assistance provided under PRISM is up to ₹15 lakh per project. 

This funding is intended to cover various aspects of product development including research and development, testing, and validation. 

The scheme is particularly focused on sectors that have high potential for innovation such as technology, healthcare, and manufacturing. 

To be eligible for the PRISM scheme, applicants must be individuals or entities classified as MSMEs. 

The definition of MSMEs is based on the investment in plant and machinery or equipment. 

For manufacturing enterprises, the investment limit is ₹10 crore for small enterprises and ₹2 crore for micro enterprises. 

For service enterprises, the investment limit is ₹5 crore for small enterprises and ₹1 crore for micro enterprises. 

Additionally, applicants must be involved in developing innovative products or services. 

The application process for the PRISM scheme involves several steps. 

First, applicants must prepare a detailed project proposal. 

This proposal should outline the innovative idea, market potential, and implementation plan. 

The proposal must also include a budget detailing how the ₹15 lakh funding will be utilized. 

Once the proposal is prepared, it should be submitted online through the official PRISM portal. 

Applicants are required to provide documents such as identity proof, address proof, and MSME registration certificate. 

After submission, the proposal will undergo a review process by a committee of experts. 

The review process typically takes about 30 to 45 days. 

If approved, the funding will be disbursed in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is usually released after the signing of a funding agreement. 

Subsequent installments are released upon the completion of specific project phases. 

The timeline for project completion under the PRISM scheme is generally set at 18 months. 

This allows sufficient time for research, development, and testing of the prototypes. 

The scheme also encourages collaboration with research institutions and universities. 

This collaboration can enhance the quality and viability of the innovations being developed. 

The PRISM scheme is part of the larger initiative by the Government of India to boost the start-up ecosystem. 

It aligns with the "Make in India" and "Start-up India" campaigns. 

These initiatives aim to create a conducive environment for entrepreneurship and innovation. 

The government has allocated a significant budget for the PRISM scheme. 

In the financial year 2021-2022, ₹100 crore was earmarked for the scheme. 

This funding is expected to increase in subsequent years as the scheme gains traction. 

The impact of the PRISM scheme can be measured through the number of successful prototypes developed. 

As of 2023, over 500 projects have received funding under the PRISM scheme. 

This has resulted in the creation of numerous innovative products that cater to various sectors. 

The scheme also aims to create job opportunities through the commercialization of these innovations. 

By supporting MSMEs, the PRISM scheme contributes to the overall economic growth of the country. 

The government has established a monitoring mechanism to track the progress of funded projects. 

This ensures accountability and transparency in the utilization of funds. 

The PRISM scheme also emphasizes the importance of intellectual property rights. 

Innovators are encouraged to file patents for their inventions to protect their ideas. 

This not only secures their innovations but also enhances their marketability. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have successfully developed their prototypes. 

Many of these innovations have gone on to receive further funding from venture capitalists. 

The PRISM scheme is a crucial step towards building a robust innovation ecosystem in India. 

It empowers individuals and small businesses to turn their ideas into reality. 

By providing financial support and mentorship, the scheme helps bridge the gap between concept and commercialization. 

The government continues to promote awareness about the PRISM scheme through workshops and seminars. 

These events aim to educate potential applicants about the benefits and application process. 

The PRISM scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to fostering innovation. 

It plays a vital role in positioning India as a global hub for technology and innovation. 

Overall, the PRISM scheme represents a significant investment in the future of Indian entrepreneurship. 

It encourages creativity and problem-solving among the youth and aspiring entrepreneurs. 

The scheme is expected to evolve further with the changing dynamics of the market. 

Future iterations may include additional support for scaling successful prototypes into full-fledged businesses. 

The PRISM scheme is a clear indication of the government's proactive approach to economic development. 

It aims to create a sustainable and self-reliant ecosystem for innovation in India. 

The success of the PRISM scheme will ultimately depend on the active participation of innovators and entrepreneurs. 

The government is committed to providing the necessary resources and support to make this initiative successful. 

In conclusion, the PRISM scheme is a vital component of India's strategy to promote innovation and entrepreneurship. 

It provides a structured framework for individuals and MSMEs to develop and commercialize their innovative ideas. 

This initiative is poised to have a lasting impact on the Indian economy and society.
